newsitem.title: USA: Apple appoints exec vp for worldwide sales.
newsitem.headline: Apple appoints exec vp for worldwide sales.

text.p: Former Apple Computer Inc. executive David Manovich will return to the struggling computer maker as executive vice president of worldwide sales and service, Apple announced Thursday.
The announcement may mark a reversal of the recent exodus from Apple's executive suit.
Manovich was formerly vice president of the Cupertino, Calif.-based company's U.S. consumer/retail sales division and most recently vice president of sales at Fujitsu PC Corp., Apple said.
He has over 14 years of sales and marketing experience in the microcomputer industry, Apple said.
Before going to Fujitsu PC, he spent over 10 years with Apple in a variety of general management and sales executive positions, the company said.

Manovich said in a statement released by the company that he wants to "help re-establish Apple's strengths in core markets" with a priority to "meet the expectations of Apple's customers and fulfil customer demand."
He added that with his previous experience at Apple, he thinks he can make "an immediate contribution."

Earlier this month, a horde of Apple executives began leaving the company -- which has seen its market share steadily eroded by machines based on Intel Corp. microprocessors running Microsoft Corp.'s Windows operating system.

On Feb. 18, Marco Landi, Apple's well-regarded executive vice president of sales, resigned. The week before, Heidi Roizen, the liaison between Apple and software companies, quit. Satjiv Chahil -- the marketing executive who got Hollywood to give starring roles to Apple's portable computers in last summer's blockbusters -- also left that week.
Last Friday, Apple squelched speculation that its chief technology officer, Ellen Hancock, would be the next to leave the company.

Landi's resignation left no top executive at Apple with more than 13 months at the company. Hancock, Chief Financial Officer Fred Anderson and Chief Administrative Officer George Scalise all joined Apple shortly after Chief Executive Gilbert Amelio replaced Michael Spindler as CEO in February 1996.
Apple stock dipped 12.5 cents to $17 on Nasdaq in morning trading.
